=== ROOT CAUSE FINDING: A MERGE COMMIT CAN NEVER BE RECORD-ONLY, SO MERGING A REVIEW RECORD INTO A BRANCH INVALIDATES THAT VERY RECORD ===

This is not a finding against PR #51. It is a defect in scripts/lwb_lanes.py on main, and I believe it is the mechanical root cause of this repository's re-cut treadmill. Found by measurement on this branch, reproduced exactly:

  commit_files() runs `git diff-tree --no-commit-id --name-only -r --root <sha>`.
  For a MERGE commit, git diff-tree with no -m/-c/--cc prints NOTHING.
  So commit_files(<any merge>) == [].
  _is_record_only_commit returns False on an empty list -- deliberately, to
  defeat the empty-commit trap its docstring names ("all() over an empty list
  is vacuously True, which would wrongly let a no-op commit skip past the walk").
  Therefore EVERY MERGE COMMIT is classified as a content commit and moves the
  reviewable head.

Measured on this branch, exactly:
  commit_files('07f82d1d...')            == []
  _is_record_only_commit('07f82d1d...')  == False
  resolve_reviewable_head(...)           == 07f82d1d...
But what 07f82d1d ACTUALLY changed relative to its first parent is:
  reviews/51/cloud-reviewer-b.json
  reviews/51/cloud-reviewer-clock-016Yb3Nh.json
and nothing else. Its own commit message says so: "Merge origin/lwb-proof-required-fail-closed (bring in both independent review records)".

So: a merge whose entire payload is two review records was classified as a content change, moved the reviewable head onto itself, and thereby made STALE both of the records it had just brought in -- including mine. The act of merging a review record destroys it. There is no exit from that loop by re-reviewing, because every subsequent merge does it again.

This is the exact defect pattern HANDOFF.md item 5 names: "I could not check" sharing a representation with "I checked and found something". `git diff-tree` returning no lines for a merge means "no combined diff to show", not "this commit changed nothing"; the code cannot tell those apart. The empty-list guard is correct for empty commits and wrong for merges, and the docstring only ever considered empty commits.

SUGGESTED FIX (offered, not applied -- my authorisation is to write reviews/<pr>/ and nothing else): in commit_files, detect a multi-parent commit and take the first-parent diff for it (`git diff-tree --no-commit-id --name-only -r -m --first-parent <sha>`, or an explicit `git diff --name-only <sha>^ <sha>` for merges), so a merge is classified by what it actually brings in. Keep the empty-list guard for genuine empty commits by distinguishing the two cases explicitly rather than by the shape of diff-tree's output. A regression test should assert that a merge bringing in only reviews/<pr>/ files is record-only, and that an empty commit still is not.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE PRs OPEN TODAY: #45, #46 and #51 are all red on lwb-lanes for staleness that this defect created or compounded, and the remedy reached for five times so far has been a full re-cut. Fixing commit_files would make merging main into a branch -- and merging reviewers' records into it -- survivable.
